analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep ... 11 Oct 2026
key_insights: Tuesday's all-time high in SPX showed the upside convexity of a market with very low net exposure. The breakout failed to hold, and index implied vols ended the week near 5-year lows, with QQQ standing out.
SPX broke through the 7800 gamma wall Tuesday morning. The first 90 minutes were the busiest for bullish activity in months, with spot up and vol up as short-dated implieds rose.

The desk lists five drivers of the Tuesday move: higher realized vol, significant call demand, underweight index exposure, clean gamma positioning, and 57 sessions left in the year with underweight positioning crowded.
SPX 1m 25 delta call implied vol was higher with spot near 7900 than with spot near 7800 later in the week.
The desk sees the marginal premium dollar more likely to chase upside through calls than to protect downside through puts.
Last quarter was the most volatile in a decade for Mag 7 names, with an 11% average realized move. Earnings season is flagged as a possible source of good news.
The index desk prefers the 30 Oct expiry. It captures the Fed, economic data and about 65% of SPX market cap reporting before 30 Oct, without paying up for the midterms.
The 102.5% call for 30 Oct expiry costs 19bps for SPY, 58bps for QQQ and 62bps for IWM.
Brazil has a key catalyst at the end of the month and the desk sees upside chase. They traded light-exotic structures and prefer EWZ higher with euro weaker as a dual.
Biotech positioning is flagged as an opportunity. The 8-week gross-down is almost without precedent.
XLU rose 4% last week but remains well off its highs, and the Street is at maximum short gamma in the sector.

New pair trade: long defense (ITA, -20% from August highs) vs short industrials ex-defense (XLI, -9% from August highs). The long leg has government-backed demand, and the short leg is exposed to rates and the cycle.
Some municipal bonds offer tax-equivalent yields near long-run equity returns of 10%+.
Outperformance options are offered as a way to get exposure to a broadening market with limited loss. They pay even if both indices fall, for example SPX -10% and RSP -3%.

Prime brokerage data show gross exposure up 3.8 points on the week (53rd percentile 1y, 80th 3y) and net exposure up 0.5 points to 46.9 (2nd percentile 1y, 4th 3y). The long/short ratio fell to a 1-year low.
One headline about AI model revenues on Thursday afternoon brought significant semis and tech supply, which the desk reads as nervous or forced length in the space.
Last quarter's earnings beats were in line with historical averages, but T+1 outperformance vs SPX was among the narrowest on record (35bps vs 95bps historically).
VIX upside convexity is extremely bid while SPX downside convexity is extremely offered. A desk colleague said a VIX above 25 feels more likely than SPX -2%.

Financials have lagged into earnings (XLF -6.5% from highs while SPX is at records). The ratio of recent drawdown to the earnings straddle is about 5x, so the implied move looks cheap. Implied moves: MS 3.7%, BAC 3.4%, WFC 4.8%.
Small-cap call demand was high this week. RTY futures positioning is at record shorts and IWM short interest is at record highs, while IWM vol is below the 10th percentile.
2026 is likely to be the most dispersive calendar year on record. The realized vol spread (average stock vs index) was 27 over the 3 months to 8 Oct and 24 over the 9 months.

The desk sees power as the most under-appreciated AI bottleneck and favors the Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW). Positioning is low, valuation has normalized, and the desk expects higher earnings revisions as independent power producers announce partnerships with mega-cap tech.

risk_factors: Fear of benchmark underperformance (FOBU) may keep investors chasing a market they are underweight.
Breakout attempts can fail to hold, as the one on Tuesday did.
Forced or nervous length in semis and tech can produce quick supply, as in the Thursday AI model revenue headline.
A correlated correction (VIX spike) is possible, otherwise a drift that lets SPX puts decay.
Financials earnings may bring larger moves than the implied levels, given the drawdown into prints.
vol_and_positioning: Index implied vols ended the week at some of the lowest levels in 5 years, with QQQ the most notable.
SPX 1m 25 delta call implied vol was higher with spot near 7900 than with spot near 7800 later in the week.
VIX upside convexity is extremely bid and SPX downside convexity is extremely offered. The desk said VIX above 25 feels more likely than SPX -2%.

PB data: gross exposure +3.8 points on the week (53rd percentile 1y, 80th 3y). Net exposure rose 0.5 points to 46.9 (2nd percentile 1y, 4th 3y). Long/short ratio (market value) fell to a 1-year low (1st percentile 5y).
Week on week, asset managers were small net sellers and hedge funds were balanced.

RTY futures positioning is at record shorts and IWM short interest is at record highs. IWM vol is below the 10th percentile. For those unwilling to cover linear, a synthetic put can be created via upside.
2026 is on track to be the most dispersive calendar year on record. The realized vol spread was 27 over the 3 months to 8 Oct and 24 over the 9 months.
The 102.5% call for 30 Oct expiry costs 19bps (SPY), 58bps (QQQ) and 62bps (IWM).
Street is at maximum short gamma in utilities (XLU).
geopolitical: Midterm elections are cited as a factor the 30 Oct expiry avoids paying up for.
Brazil has a key catalyst at the end of the month, not specified further in the report.
